questions.q: Why does a model need positions at all?
options: Attention alone gives the same result, just reordered, whichever way tokens are shuffled
Tokens have no channels otherwise
The VAE requires them
They speed up the sampler
questions.answer: Attention alone gives the same result, just reordered, whichever way tokens are shuffled
questions.why: The lab's first line shows it.

questions.q: Why use many frequencies rather than one?
options: One wave repeats, so far positions can look alike
One frequency costs more memory
Sine is undefined at large numbers
More frequencies remove the need for heads
questions.answer: One wave repeats, so far positions can look alike
questions.why: Try the play: with one frequency, positions 44 apart nearly match. Longer waves separate them.

questions.q: How does a 2D table get made from 1D codes?
options: Half the width for rows, half for columns, then join
Multiply a row code by a column code
Average the two codes
Use only the row code
questions.answer: Half the width for rows, half for columns, then join

questions.q: FLUX has no position table. What does it use?
options: Ids per token that become rotations
A learned table per resolution
No position at all
The seed
questions.answer: Ids per token that become rotations
questions.why: process_img builds img_ids, and EmbedND makes rotations from them.

questions.q: Why does a change of image size need a rule for a table but not for RoPE ids?
options: A table has a fixed grid, while ids are just computed for any token
RoPE only works at one size
Tables are learned from the prompt
Ids are stored in the checkpoint
questions.answer: A table has a fixed grid, while ids are just computed for any token
questions.why: A table covers one grid, so PixArt rescales its coordinates. RoPE needs only ids.
